United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative:
Over the past decade, the Moroccan ministry of education established an enabling environment to ensure a transformative education system. Sustainable development was integrated in the school curriculum, and efforts have been made invested towards integrating the ecological programme and ensuring the upgrade of environmental rural schools. Both initiatives aimed at promoting environmental and sustainable development education; mobilizing teachers and students to address environmental issues; and establishing educational and awareness raising programs in schools. Furthermore, Morocco has demonstrated its commitment to greening education by signing the Greening Education Partnership. Additionally, the country is a founding partner of the Declaration on the Common Agenda for Education and Climate Change voiced at COP28, which reinforces its dedication to integrate climate education and sustainability into its educational framework. Despite the efforts invested by the ministry of education, a multifaceted and multilayered approach is needed to curb the environmental crisis at various territorial scales in Morocco. National assessments underscore the critical situation which is marked by an unprecedented natural resources degradation. These studies reveal unhealthy living conditions due to air pollution, inland and marine waters contamination, desertification, forest, and biodiversity losses.
The Moroccan government acknowledging the alarming state of the environment, has recently focused on upgrading climate change and environmental education programs. The national sewage programme, the national household waste management programme, and the Maroc Vert were launched. Though, it is revealed that education for sustainable development and climate change remains at the heart of reshaping the behaviors of new generations, to become the future stewards of natural resources and biodiversity.
In this context, the project will capitalize on the processes that motivate kids and adolescents to explore the emerging environmental crisis, and engage them in activities that trigger critical thinking, and strengthen problem solving skills. The activities will aim to transform the future generation to be ‘responsible citizens’, well equipped for a better ‘greener’ future of the Earth. It will also co-create ‘homesteads’ at schools in the urban gardens, co-conceived and planted by the whole schools communities, including teachers and students. The targeted group includes teachers, students, and their communities. The project will be implemented at pre-selected schools, through the establishment of urban school gardens, in partnership with UNESCO biosphere reserves and global geoparks in Morocco. The project activities will address [1] raising awareness of the targeted groups to acquire better understanding of the environmental crisis and its challenges, [2] gain the knowledge through information about biodiversity conservation, climate change and sustainable development, [3] instill attitudes of concern among the new generation, and [4] acquire problem-solving skills to identify and address environmental challenges on daily basis.
The project major outcome is a Greening Education Model to be replicated in other pioneer schools in other cities in Morocco, and in the Maghreb region in the future. The trained teachers and students will constitute the first cohort to lead the replication, adaptation and implementation of peer education projects. - Greening education in pilot schools in Rabat, in cooperation with UNESCO biosphere reserves and global geoparks, through the establishment of urban school’s gardens. - Develop capacities of teachers and co-produce knowledge and promotional products for teachers and trainers. - Sensibilization of teachers, students and the students’ community on sustainable development, biodiversity conservation and climate change.
